title: The Dishwasher: Dead Samurai
subtitle: A dishwasher fights through a hand-drawn nightmare

body: The Dishwasher: Dead Samurai is James Silva's side-scrolling action game for Xbox Live Arcade, released on 1 April 2009. An unnamed dishwasher battles through waves of enemies using increasingly elaborate weapons and combinations. Its scratchy, hand-drawn appearance gives the violent action a restless visual identity. The player begins with meat cleavers before acquiring equipment that changes the possibilities within a fight. A level becomes a continuous effort to connect attacks, stay mobile and recognise when a weakened opponent can be finished before the next group closes in.

Basic attacks, stronger strikes and grabs can be linked into combinations, while vulnerable enemies allow finishing moves that provide additional points and health. Defeated opponents leave spirals that support upgrades, and later weapons include a katana, firearms and a chainsaw. Dish Magic adds another resource to the available responses. The player has to make those tools work together against groups rather than treating each enemy as an isolated duel. A good sequence creates space, rewards the finishing blow and places the character where the next attack can begin without losing momentum.

Silva's idea grew from his own work as a dishwasher and eventually took shape using XNA Game Studio Express. Winning Microsoft's 2007 Dream-Build-Play competition brought a publishing contract for Xbox Live Arcade. Challenge and Arcade modes concentrate the combat into different arrangements, while cooperative play allows other players to join the action. A guitar minigame even supports familiar music-game peripherals. The game's arrival demonstrated how an individual creator could use accessible development tools and a digital console storefront to bring a strongly personal visual style and demanding action system to a broad audience.
